idiom_name: hylo alg coalg = unfold then fold in a single recursion (cata alg . ana coalg)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: fix the base functor F shared by both halves, write the coalgebra as seed -> F seed (with a terminal case) and the algebra as F result -> result, then implement the driver as one recursion that applies the coalgebra, recurses into the produced successors and applies the algebra on the way back, so the intermediate F-tree never exists - hylo alg coalg = cata alg . ana coalg. In strict languages without a lazy iteration protocol this is either a single-pass loop that carries the accumulator beside the seed or an explicit hand-written recursion; in languages with laziness it is the generator/iterator composed with the fold. GHC can deforest the intermediate structure but the resulting fused code is not automatically tail-recursive; use an explicit accumulator in the algebra for constant space. Use the Haskell recursion-schemes library (Data.Functor.Foldable) for hylo, refold, and generalized variants (hyloM for monadic effects, elgotHylo for early exit, ghyloW for comonad-wrapped fusion). In Scala use Matryoshka (hyloF for pure, hyloM for monadic, elgotHylo/ghyoW for advanced forms). In Rust use ordofp::recursion::hylo or karpal-recursion for hylo plus histo, futu, chrono; refold in semi_persistent_traversals for a simple refold.
code_sketch:
# alg : F b -> b, coalg : a -> F a, seed : a
hylo(alg, coalg, seed) = alg(map(lambda child: hylo(alg, coalg, child), coalg(seed)))
# strict form (fused loop):
for s in unfold_steps(seed):            # coalgebra
    acc = alg(acc, s)                   # algebra, same iteration
pitfalls: Implementing the unfold and the fold as two passes (materialize, then consume) and still calling it a hylomorphism.
Ignoring the stack: eliminating the structure replaces heap with recursion depth.
Fusing a coalgebra and an algebra over different shapes and ad-hoc buffering the difference - the intermediate structure has only been renamed.
Assuming deforestation is tail-safe: in GHC the fused hylo is not tail-recursive; an explicit accumulator in the algebra is needed for constant space.
Using a recursive functor as its own base functor (e.g., [] instead of a non-recursive ListF) can cause non-termination on corner cases.
Forgetting to INLINE the catamorphism wrapper when using generic recursion-schemes; GHC cannot otherwise fuse the fmap layers, defeating deforestation.

Confusing hylomorphism (cata . ana = unfold then fold) with metamorphism (ana . cata = fold then unfold): the two operators compose in opposite directions and produce fundamentally different programs.

Violating the Functor law requirement of the base functor: fmap must satisfy identity (fmap id = id) and composition (fmap (f . g) = fmap f . fmap g); a broken fmap causes silent incorrectness in the fused recursion.

Thunk build-up in lazy languages: when the fold half is strict in its recursive argument but the coalgebra produces lazy fields, unevaluated thunks accumulate on the heap, and the fused form can use more memory than the materialised two-phase version.

Assuming the GHC INLINE heuristic works uniformly: hyloM (monadic hylomorphism) and elgotHylo require different inlining strategies than the plain hylo; consult the recursion-schemes library haddock before applying the vanilla catamorphism pragma guidance.

Using a hylomorphism when the intermediate structure must be shared by multiple consumers: the fusion destroys all sharing; instead keep the materialised intermediate and fold it multiple times, or switch to an explicit memoised refold.

Wrong move: wrap an already-fused native pipeline (a Rust iterator chain, a Python generator feeding sum(), a LINQ query) in hand-rolled Fix/BaseFunctor hylo machinery -> the coalgebra/algebra vocabulary adds reading cost while saving zero allocations -> instead keep the language's lazy pipeline and reserve the named scheme for shapes it cannot fuse.

Wrong move: implement hylo with the textbook algebra-map form (map the recursive call over the functor layer on the way back up) and assume the fmap is free -> every layer allocates a functor wrapper on the way down and on the way up, which can cost more than the two-pass version -> instead use the fmap-free hylo' form where the algebra receives already-folded children directly, or the library's optimized driver.

Wrong move: validate a fused hylomorphism against the two-phase version only on small inputs -> fusion trades heap for stack and can additionally leak thunks under laziness, neither of which shows at toy sizes -> instead benchmark production-sized and adversarially deep inputs, tracking peak heap and maximum stack depth separately.
sources: Meijer, Fokkinga & Paterson, Functional Programming with Bananas, Lenses, Envelopes and Barbed Wire (FPCA 1991) — the paper that introduced catamorphisms, anamorphisms and hylomorphisms (refolds). https://maartenfokkinga.github.io/utwente/mmf91m.pdf

Hinze, Wu & Gibbons, Conjugate Hylomorphisms — Or: The Mother of All Structured Recursion Schemes (POPL 2015) — unifies folds, unfolds, paramorphisms, histomorphisms, futumorphisms, apomorphisms and zygomorphisms under the conjugate rule. https://doi.org/10.1145/2676726.2676989

Hinze & Wu, Unifying Structured Recursion Schemes (JFP 2015) — shows how adjoint folds subsume comonad-based recursion schemes. https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/S0956796815000258
Gibbons, Calculating Functional Programs (2002) — derivation and calculation with recursion schemes including hylomorphisms. https://cs.ox.ac.uk/jeremy.gibbons/publications/

Yang & Wu, Fantastic Morphisms and Where to Find Them: A Guide to Recursion Schemes (MPC 2022) — practical, example-driven survey of hylomorphisms and related schemes. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-16912-0_9

Hinze, Histo- and Dynamorphisms Revisited (WGP 2013) — dynamic programming via histomorphisms and dynamorphisms; relates to hylomorphisms for tabulation. https://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/ralf.hinze/publications/WGP13.pdf

Primitive (Co)Recursion and Course-of-Value (Co)Iteration, Categorically (Informatica 2020) — surveys histomorphisms, futumorphisms, paramorphisms, apomorphisms and their categorical models. https://informatica.vu.lt/journal/INFORMATICA/article/256/file/pdf
jtobin.io, Practical Recursion Schemes (2016) — industry-oriented introduction with mergesort hylo example and production context. https://jtobin.io/practical-recursion-schemes

Blog.sumtypeofway.com, Recursion Schemes Part V: Hello Hylomorphisms — accessible walkthrough with RPN calculator and edit-distance examples. https://blog.sumtypeofway.com/posts/recursion-schemes-part-5.html

Bartosz Milewski, Stalking a Hylomorphism in the Wild (2017) — category-theory-grounded introduction with concrete applications. https://bartoszmilewski.com/2017/12/29/stalking-a-hylomorphism-in-the-wild/

Newartisans.com, Lost in Technopolis: A Win for Recursion Schemes (2018) — industry experience report using nixpkgs and recursion schemes including hylomorphisms. https://newartisans.com/2018/04/win-for-recursion-schemes/

Hackage, Data.Functor.Foldable (recursion-schemes library) — Haskell library documentation for hylo, refold, hyloM, elgotHylo, ghyloW and related schemes. https://hackage.haskell.org/package/recursion-schemes/docs/Data-Functor-Foldable.html
Matryoshka (Scala) — hyloF, hyloM, elgotHylo, ghyloW, chronoF for effectful and comonadic hylomorphisms. https://github.com/precog/matryoshka
ordofp/recursion Rust crate — hylo with FunctorHKT, factorial example. https://docs.rs/ordofp/latest/ordofp/recursion/fn.hylo.html
karpal-recursion Rust crate — hylo, cata, ana, para, apo, histo, futu, zygo, chrono for Rust. https://docs.rs/crate/karpal-recursion/latest

Wiley Software journal, Solving Dynamic Programming Problems in Haskell by Memoization of Hylomorphisms (2019) — memoized hylo for CYK, knapsack; fusion + tabulation. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/spe.2887
Stack Overflow, Deforestation in a Hylomorphism — GHC fusion is not tail-recursive; accumulator pattern required. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49135351/deforestation-in-a-hylomorphism

Stack Overflow, Is it possible to make GHC optimize (deforest) generic catamorphisms? — INLINE pragma needed on catam to enable GHC fusion. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13099203/is-it-possible-to-make-ghc-optimize-deforest-generic-functions-such-as-catamor

higherkindness/droste — Scala recursion schemes for Cats: ghylo/hylo over fixed-point types with athema (a math-expression parser) as a worked hylomorphism example. https://github.com/higherkindness/droste

retro-freedom.nz, Haskell Magic: Making hylos faster — replaces the fmap-based textbook hylo with the fmap-free hylo' from Bananas in Space, cutting per-layer functor allocation. https://retro-freedom.nz/haskell-magic-making-hylos-faster.html
